6.4a — Boots: Double Jump

The axe granted an attack. The potion capped a number. The boots grant movement — a second jump mid-air — and that one item restructures your whole level design, because every gap, wall, and secret is now jumpable twice. Capability items rewrite the world.

Predict First ~10 min

You already know the shape (5.1a): pickup → bool → capability. Predict the three pieces before writing them:

PieceYour prediction
Inventory fieldprivate bool ___ = false
Pickup branchCompareTag("___") → set true, Destroy
Jump logic??? — and HERE is the new question: how do you count jumps in mid-air?

The trap: isGrounded (from 6.2a) can answer "may I jump?" but not "is this my FIRST or SECOND jump?" Mid-air, grounded is false for both. You need a counter — jumps used — that resets when you land. Predict its type, its reset point, and the exact condition:

if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Space) && ??? )
{
    ???
}

Socratic

A bool says one jump; a counter says any number of jumps; the AP exam says: choose the abstraction that matches the problem. If your game later adds WING BOOTS for a third jump, which of your lines changes — and which one sentence would you write for the Create PT to justify this data choice?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — the counter. Add to PlayerController, in the starter's voice:

[SerializeField] private int maxJumps = 1;   // boots raise this
private int jumpsUsed;

// reset the moment you touch ground (right where isGrounded is set):
if (isGrounded) jumpsUsed = 0;

// the jump condition becomes:
if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Space) && jumpsUsed < maxJumps)
{
    rb.AddForce(Vector2.up * jumpForce, ForceMode2D.Impulse);
    jumpsUsed++;
}

Run it: still one jump (1 used < 1 max). The counter exists but changes nothing yet — deploy code in neutral, THEN flip the switch. That order keeps bugs boring.

Step 2 — the boots. Build the pickup exactly like the axe: sprite (a boot!), trigger collider, tag "Boots" (make the tag), and the branch:

if (other.CompareTag("Boots"))
{
    maxJumps = 2;
    // animator swap / particle flourish here if you have art
    Destroy(other.gameObject);
}

Press Play: one jump. Grab the boots. Two jumps. Now the LEVEL is different — every gap you tuned in 6.1a just became trivial. Hold that thought for Step 4.

Step 3 — merge with the mercies. Your jump condition from 6.3a had coyote time and a buffer in it. Careful surgery: the buffer should NOT fire the second jump while you fall (buffer was for landing). Decide: second jump must be a DIRECT press in the air. Write the full condition: (grounded OR coyote) AND count-ok for the first; NOT grounded AND count-ok for the second. Test both jumps with late presses and early presses at a ledge edge. If it feels wrong, your two timer-paths are fighting — print them.

Step 4 — redesign for capability. Place a coin where ONLY a double jump reaches. Now the level has a soft gate: no damage, no lock — just a visible "come back when you are more." That is a metroidvania in one sentence. The boots are not a power-up; they are a KEY made of physics.

Bug Hunt: The infinite stair

  1. Put maxJumps = 2 in the field's starting value (serialized!). The whole cave is now jumpable without boots — what "cost" did forgetting the default destroy?
  2. Reset jumpsUsed in Update instead of where isGrounded is set. Where does the reset happen when you are FALLING (isGrounded false) — and why is the second jump... not second?
  3. Grab the boots TWICE (two pickups on the map). maxJumps becomes 2 then 2. Should the second pair do NOTHING, or is there a design where stacking makes sense (3 jumps)? Who decides — code or designer?
  4. Second jump with FULL jumpForce feels like a stutter-step. Try 0.8 × jumpForce for the air jump. Which line needs to know WHICH jump number it is?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Capability design

  1. Design a THIRD item (gloves → wall jump?) using the same pickup skeleton. What does the LEVEL gain access to — write two sentences like a designer selling it.
  2. Make the boots REQUIRED: seal the cave exit behind a high ledge. What does the player do when they hit the ledge before the boots — and is that frustration or curiosity?
  3. Commit + push: "6.4a: double jump + soft gate".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain counter vs bool for multi-jump and why the counter resets on landing
  • Build the boots pickup and raise maxJumps
  • Merge the counter with coyote/buffer without the buffer double-firing
  • Design a soft gate (visible, unreachable, no damage)
